About

A republic of three islands, drawn by hand

Vaelora is an invented archipelago nation in the warm northern sea. This atlas is a fully interactive map of it — and a small demonstration that a real pan-and-zoom mapping experience can be built from nothing but vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

The nation of Vaelora

Vaelora spans three islands. Maelan, the largest, holds four of the six provinces: the terraced vineyards of Sundermark, the harbour metropolis of Aevenport, the reed-marshes of Morrowfen, and the rain-soaked western forests of Kelvarne. Off the south-east lies the young volcanic island of Taleth, crowned by smoking Mount Vey; and far to the north, the windswept skerries of Orrin Holm guard the approaches with a single iron lighthouse.

The republic is stitched together by the Vaeloran Tramway — three coloured lines (Amber, Teal and Violet) meeting at Aeven Quay — and the old Coast Highway, Route 1, which runs the length of Maelan. None of these places exist; every coastline, river, road and station below was drawn coordinate by coordinate.

The map engine

The explorer is a genuine "slippy map" with no Leaflet, Mapbox, D3 or tiles of any kind. The world is a fixed 1000×700 coordinate space; the camera is described by a view rectangle that becomes the SVG viewBox, so the browser maps world coordinates to the screen for us while panning and zooming stay mathematically exact.

  • Pan & zoomPointer-drag to pan; wheel / pinch to zoom centred on the cursor; double-click to zoom in. The view is clamped to bounds and a min/max zoom.
  • Toggleable layersRegions, water, roads, the tramway, points of interest, labels and a coordinate grid can each be shown or hidden independently.
  • Decluttered labelsLabels appear by zoom level and are removed by screen-space collision so the map never overcrowds.
  • Hit-testingCustom point-in-polygon and nearest-point tests power hover highlighting, tooltips and click-to-select — no invisible DOM overlays.
  • Route plannerPick two tram stations and Dijkstra's algorithm walks the line graph to draw the shortest path, with distance, stop count and interchanges.
  • Search & fly-toA filterable list of every place animates the camera to the selection with an eased fly-to.
  • Minimap & scaleAn overview inset shows the live viewport rectangle; a scale bar and lat/long readout track the cursor.
  • PersistenceYour theme, layer choices and last viewport are saved to localStorage and restored on return.

Controls

  • Mouse / touchDrag to pan · wheel or pinch to zoom · double-click to zoom in (shift double-click to zoom out) · click a feature for details.
  • Keyboard↑↓←→ pan · + / − zoom · 0 fit · Esc close panel · Enter on a focused feature opens it.
  • MinimapClick or drag inside the overview inset to recenter the main map.
